headline: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the United States and China are likely to agree on a way to warn each other about serious AI accidents.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the interview dates from 3 Oct, before the 4 Oct cutoff, and only a relayed account was read.
importance_line: Could create a first US-China channel for AI incidents, but it is only a US proposal that Bessent expects to be accepted, and Trump said last week he does not want an AI safety deal with China.
summary: Axios reported, in an interview with Bessent published on 3 Oct, that the US plans to propose a system for alerting China to serious AI incidents, and Digitimes reports that Bessent expects Washington and Beijing to agree on it. Bessent raised AI risks such as rogue AI agents with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in September, while saying the labs, not the government, must manage the risks of their own models.
notes: Read The Next Web (relaying Axios) plus the opening of the Digitimes page; Axios original not opened, so the source is Axios via two relays. Follow-up of yesterday's pool story.
